p01.why: The operators work on two's complement bits, so -1 & 0xFF is 255, -8 | 1 is -7, -1 ^ 1 is -2, and ~-1 is 0.

p02.why: & binds tighter than ^, which binds tighter than |, and == binds tighter than all three, so each assertion holds; the warnings stay warnings without -Werror.

p03.why: A floating-point operand is not valid for &.

p04.why: Scoped enumeration operands are not valid for | without an operator function.

p05.why: S has no conversion and no operator&, so the class operand is not valid.

p06.why: A pointer operand is not valid for |.

p07.why: A pointer-to-member operand is not valid for ^.

p08.why: The values match the page's examples: 2, 7, 5, -1, -6.

p09.why: Unscoped enumerations, bool, char, and long are valid operands, and the values are 3, 1, 1, and 4.

p10.why: ~ on a bool draws a -Wbool-operation warning, which -Werror makes an error.

p11.why: a & b == c has a comparison as an operand of & without parentheses, so -Wparentheses warns and -Werror makes it an error.

p12.why: ~ does not accept a floating-point operand.

p13.why: nullptr is not a valid operand of |.

p14.why: Two different unscoped enumerations are valid operands; the deprecation warning stays a warning without -Werror.

p15.why: true promotes to int 1, so ~true is -2 and ~false is -1; the warning is off by default.

p16.why: Mixing two enumeration types draws -Wdeprecated-enum-enum-conversion, which -Werror makes an error.

p17.why: The parentheses make the intent explicit, so no -Wparentheses warning is given.

p18.why: ~ on an int is not on a bool, so -Wbool-operation does not warn.

p19.why: unsigned char 0 promotes to int, so ~zero is -1, and ~0u is the largest unsigned value.

p20.why: char, bool, unsigned char, and the unscoped enum promote to int, u & 1 is unsigned, and l | 1 is long.

p21.why: &x is a pointer, which ~ does not accept.
